gaps.sentence: We will refund the item provided that you ___ the receipt.
gaps.hint: provided that plus a present requirement
gaps.explanation: 'Provided that' states a requirement using the present simple: have.

gaps.sentence: ___ harder, she would have passed the exam.
gaps.hint: inversion replaces if in formal English
gaps.explanation: Formal English can drop 'if' and invert: Had she studied harder, she would have passed.

gaps.sentence: You can stay out late as long as you ___ me a text when you arrive.
gaps.hint: as long as plus present simple
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: send.

gaps.sentence: I will be surprised if he ___ on time for once.
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a real future condition takes the present simple: arrives.

gaps.sentence: Unless you ___ the exact change, the machine will not accept it.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' states the condition that must be met and takes the present simple: have.

gaps.sentence: I'd have helped if I ___ about the problem.
gaps.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + participle.

gaps.sentence: If people ___ less time on their phones, they would read more.
gaps.explanation: An unreal present habit takes the past simple in the if-clause: spent.

gaps.sentence: I wish you ___ so pessimistic about the project.
gaps.hint: a wish about a present attitude
gaps.explanation: Wishes about present states use 'were': were not.
